message.text: Why is the com.google.gson.Gson import not working?

reply.text:
Most likely the Gson JAR isn't on the classpath for the project/test, so Eclipse can't resolve `import com.google.gson.Gson;`. Possible causes and fixes:

- Dependency not declared in your build (Maven/Gradle) — add Gson to `pom.xml` or `build.gradle`.
- Wrong dependency scope (`provided`) or missing `testImplementation` for test-only usage.
- Maven/Gradle project not refreshed in Eclipse — run Maven -> Update Project or Gradle -> Refresh.
- Using Java modules (`module-info.java`) — ensure the module requires the Gson module (check the JAR's `Automatic-Module-Name`).
- If not using a build tool, add the gson JAR to the project's Build Path (Project -> Properties -> Java Build Path -> Libraries).

Maven (add to `pom.xml`):
```xml
<!-- Add this inside <dependencies> -->
<dependency>
  <groupId>com.google.code.gson</groupId>
  <artifactId>gson</artifactId>
  <version>2.8.9</version>
  <!-- use <scope>test</scope> only if you need it just for tests -->
</dependency>
```

Gradle (Groovy DSL, add to `build.gradle`):
```gradle
// For main code
implementation 'com.google.code.gson:gson:2.8.9'

// For tests only
testImplementation 'com.google.code.gson:gson:2.8.9'
```

After adding the dependency, in Eclipse: right‑click the project -> Maven -> Update Project (or Gradle -> Refresh) and then clean/build. If you use `module-info.java`, add the appropriate `requires` entry for the Gson module.
